brief: Goldman's Rikin Shah argues rates are stuck between an AI-driven equity drawdown and an energy shock, with the Fed and ECB the only source of calm. Both paused this week (Fed 10-2, with two hawkish dissents; ECB pausing as Lagarde's February exit nears) even as euro-area inflation is priced at 4.5% by Q1 and the September US core print ran hot, because the Nasdaq's near-9% drop and wider credit spreads are feeding their reaction function; December hikes stay live. The correlation regime has flipped: 10Y Treasury moves now track the Nasdaq (+0.60) rather than oil (-0.28), so Treasuries rallied Friday even as Brent hit $118 and the Nasdaq fell 3.5%. Separately, European gas broke above €100/MWh on 14-year-low storage and Hormuz LNG flows stuck near 20-25% of pre-war levels, short of the 65% Goldman's base case needs; its risk matrix spans €70-€150 depending on Hormuz and winter weather. The UK's low-drama budget supports gilts ahead of a near-fully-priced BoE hike. Shah distrusts the calm; the piece argues oil, not AI, is more likely to force central banks' hand first.
